sourceInformation.source: Pressure Cooker (1983), Activision; original arcade cooking reinterpretation. Specific source details beyond native model knowledge: unknown.
sourceInformation.genre: Arcade action; cooking and time management
sourceInformation.tech: Three.js 0.180.0 / R180; WebGPURenderer with WebGPU and WebGL 2 fallback; Rapier 3D 0.19.3; Gamepad API; Web Audio API; AI Hub session client 1.4.0 / protocol v1; esbuild 0.25.12. All runtime dependencies embedded.
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural cel-shaded diner diorama, ink outlines, warm paper, terracotta and mint palette.
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer and AnimationClip with authored breathing, walking, spatula flick, serve jump and customer idle tracks; procedural food and effect motion.
sourceInformation.audio: Code-generated swung diner jazz, synthesized effects and pitched Animalese/Simlish-style gibberish. No audio files. Music defaults to 10%.
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub synchronized parallel score attack, 1–4 players; standalone solo and 1–2 player couch co-op. No standalone remote matchmaking.
sourceInformation.testing: 110/110 automated checks passed: cooking rules, complete three-rush campaign with native physics, keyboard/mouse, two emulated standard gamepads, touch, sampled Web Audio output, GPU-loss recovery, and AI Hub conformance (2 players; 4 players with 150 ms latency, 50 ms jitter and 5% loss; host departure). Layouts reviewed at 1920×1080 and 390×844 through WebGL 2; healthy WebGPU state checked directly because headless captures can be blank. Physical hardware and actual listening: unknown.
sourceInformation.research: No internet search. Source design uses native model knowledge. Supplied AI Hub protocol/client/harness fetched directly; pinned npm dependencies downloaded.
sourceInformation.environment: Codex CLI (headless); Linux / Ubuntu 26.04 on WSL2

testingFeedback: 4 game/UX issues found during testing and review: graphics-loss recovery, live ticket-patience reset synchronization, title/mobile layout wrapping, and co-op collider spawn alignment. Test-driver fixes were tracked separately.
1 potentially game-breaking issue: losing the WebGPU device could leave a blank kitchen. Automatic WebGL 2 recovery now preserves the game state and passed deliberate device-loss testing.

The scripted full three-rush playthrough with native Rapier physics, followed by the supplied AI Hub harness under four-player network impairment and host departure. The final suite passed 110/110 checks.
The first headless WebGPU screenshots. A blank capture could not distinguish a rendering failure from a screenshot limitation, so direct device-state checks and WebGL layout captures were needed.
engineFeedback: Native toon materials, orthographic cameras, and AnimationMixer clips made the illustrated diner and expressive chef animation straightforward.

promptFeedback: The concrete source, art direction, control philosophy, attract-mode requirement and single-file deliverable supported a coherent complete arcade game.

aiHub.name: Pressure Griller
aiHub.tagline: A little lunch. A lot of hustle.
aiHub.description: Catch conveyor toppings, stack the regulars’ burgers and hustle to the right counter in an inked 3D diner. Beat three escalating lunch rushes solo, share a kitchen with a friend, or compete for tips in AI Hub.
aiHub.controls: Move: left stick / WASD. Catch or serve: Cross / Space. Dash: Circle / Shift. Bell: Triangle / Q. Ticket: R1 / Tab. Clear tray: Square / R. P2: arrows / Enter. Touch: drag, assisted catching.
